title: What Time Is It?
subtitle: Four conversations about the time
review: Text from time.md; notes and questions written by Claude. No Burmese yet.
intro: Emma asks the time at a bus stop, plans a film with Lucas, tells him he is late for class, and Lucas buys a train ticket from an agent. Listen for the time in each conversation, then say it with them.

lines.text: Excuse me. Do you have the time, please?
lines.note: A polite way to ask a stranger the time. It means: What time is it?

lines.text: Yes, of course. It's ten fifteen.
lines.note: 10:15. You can also say a quarter past ten.

lines.text: Ten fifteen? Already?
Yes. Are you in a hurry?
A little. My bus leaves at twenty past ten.
lines.note: 10:20. at + a time: at twenty past ten.

lines.text: Then you'd better hurry! The bus stop is right there.
Thank you. Have a nice day!
Shall we go to the movies tonight?
Good idea! What time does the film start?
At half past eight.
lines.note: 8:30. You can also say eight thirty.

lines.text: And what time shall we meet?
At quarter to eight, outside the cinema?
lines.note: 7:45. to = before: fifteen minutes before eight.

lines.text: Quarter to eight. OK.
Great. See you tonight!
Emma, what time is it?
It's ten to nine.
What? Already? I'm late!
What time does your class start?
At nine o'clock sharp.
lines.note: o'clock is only for the exact hour. Sharp = exactly, not one minute later.

lines.text: Then you've got ten minutes. Hurry!
I'm off. See you later!
Good afternoon. What time does the next train to New York leave?
At two thirty-five, from platform three.
lines.note: 2:35. After half past, we often just say the numbers: two thirty-five.

lines.text: And what time does it arrive?
At four forty.
lines.note: 4:40. Four forty, or twenty to five.

lines.text: Perfect. And what time is it now?
It's ten past two. You've got twenty-five minutes.
Great. One ticket, please.

questions.q: What time does Emma's bus leave?
questions.why: Emma says: My bus leaves at twenty past ten.

questions.q: What time do Emma and Lucas meet outside the cinema?
questions.why: Lucas says: At quarter to eight, outside the cinema. The film starts at half past eight.

questions.q: Emma says: It's ten to nine. What time is it?
questions.why: Ten to nine = ten minutes before nine.

questions.q: It's ten past two. The train leaves at two thirty-five. How long does Lucas have?

notes: What time is it? / Do you have the time? ask for the time now. The answer starts with It's: It's ten to nine.
What time does the film start? asks when something happens. The answer uses at: At half past eight.
past = after the hour: twenty past ten (10:20), ten past two (2:10).
to = before the next hour: quarter to eight (7:45), ten to nine (8:50).
You can also say the numbers: ten fifteen (10:15), two thirty-five (2:35), four forty (4:40).
o'clock is only for the exact hour: nine o'clock, but half past nine.
